title: Regular Verbs
sourceNote: The auto-captions are heavily garbled; the verb forms are standard German, but the exercise sentences at the end were reconstructed from context.
objectives: I can conjugate regular verbs in the present tense
I can handle stems ending in s, ß, z, d or t
I can use common regular verbs in sentences

patterns.ex: ich wohne, du wohnst, er wohnt
patterns.en: I live, you live, he lives

grammar.title: The regular endings
grammar.body: Regular verbs (*regelmäßige* or *schwache Verben*) keep their stem. You only add the ending that fits the pronoun. Notice that *er / sie / es* and *ihr* have the same ending **-t**, and *wir* and *sie / Sie* have the same ending **-en** (identical to the infinitive).
grammar.ar: الأفعال المنتظمة: نضيف النهاية إلى الجذع فقط.

grammar.title: More regular verbs
grammar.body: All these verbs follow the same pattern. Listen and repeat: *ich studiere, du studierst, er studiert; ich höre, du hörst, er hört; ich frage, du fragst, er fragt; ich sage, du sagst, er sagt.*

grammar.title: Special case 1: stems ending in -s, -ß, -z
grammar.body: If the stem already ends in an s-sound (**s, ß, z**), the *du* form only takes **-t**, not *-st*. This avoids a double s-sound.

grammar.title: Special case 2: stems ending in -d or -t
grammar.body: If the stem ends in **-d** or **-t**, you add an extra **e** before *-st* and *-t*, so the verb is easy to pronounce: *du arbeitest*, *er arbeitet*, *ihr arbeitet*. The same applies to *warten*.
grammar.ar: إذا انتهى الجذع بـ d أو t نضيف e قبل st و t.

mistakes.why: The stem ends in s, so du takes only -t.
Stems in -t need an extra e: *arbeitest*.
*er / sie / es* needs -t, and the stem in -t needs the extra e.

pronunciation.tip: In *du arbeitest* you clearly hear the extra *e*: ar-bai-test.

lines.de: Ich arbeite bei Siemens. Und du?
lines.en: I work at Siemens. And you?

lines.de: Ich studiere Mathematik. Ich wohne in Köln.
lines.en: I study maths. I live in Cologne.
Does Veronika also live in Cologne?

lines.de: Ja, sie wohnt auch in Köln.
lines.en: Yes, she also lives in Cologne.

tip: Do not worry about the long lists. With practice the endings become automatic: ich -e, du -st, er -t, wir -en, ihr -t, sie -en.

comprehension.q: Does the stem of a regular verb change?
Which two pronouns have the ending -t?
What happens with *du* when the stem ends in s, ß or z?
comprehension.a: It takes only -t (du reist, du tanzt).

comprehension.q: What happens with *du* when the stem ends in -d or -t?

exercises.instructions: Write the correct form of the verb in brackets.

exercises.instructions: Choose the correct form for du.

summary: Regular verbs keep their stem; add: ich -e, du -st, er/sie/es -t, wir -en, ihr -t, sie/Sie -en.
Stems in -s, -ß, -z: du takes only -t (du reist, du tanzt, du heißt).
Stems in -d or -t: add an extra e (du arbeitest, er arbeitet, ihr wartet).
Learn the pattern, not every verb separately.
